mainTopic: Conditional חטאות, a נזיר's set-aside money, and מעילה with blood and נסכים
overview: The amud opens with the end of a משנה about חטאות. When the owner has not yet gotten his כפרה, the animal grazes until it gets a מום and is sold, and it still makes a תמורה and has מעילה. The גמרא explains why the משנה splits only the last cases: their rule depends on the owner's כפרה. It also explains why the same משנה appears both in מסכת תמורה and here. A new משנה teaches that money a נזיר set aside for his offerings without dividing it up may not be used, but has no מעילה, because every coin could go to the שלמים. It also rules on what happens to his money if he dies. ריש לקיש asks why the משנה did not teach the same rule for bird-offering money, and רבא answers that the Torah never calls for unfit birds. A third משנה, from רבי שמעון, teaches that blood is lenient at first and strict at the end, while נסכים are the opposite. The גמרא brings a dispute about מעילה with blood and gives sources for the view that it has none. It then challenges רבי יוחנן's source, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The owner has not yet achieved atonement: the animal grazes, is sold, and keeps its holiness
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes the case of the two 'conditional' חטאות: if the owner has not yet gotten his כפרה, the animal grazes until it gets a מום, is sold, and the money buys a new קרבן. Meanwhile it can make a תמורה and has מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the owners have not yet achieved atonement, the animal should graze until it gets a blemish. Then it is sold, and they buy another animal with its money. It can make a substitute, and someone who benefits from it is guilty of misusing holy property.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה. It gives the ruling for when the owner of the sin offering has not yet gotten his כפרה through a different animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the owner still needs a קרבן, this animal is not sent to die. Its value is turned into a new קרבן instead. Because it still has real holiness, an animal exchanged for it becomes a תמורה, and using it for yourself is מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: The owners achieved atonement (through another offering)
It grazes until it gets a blemish (מום) and can no longer be offered
Its money: what it is sold for
Substitution: trying to swap a regular animal for a holy one, which makes the new animal holy too
Misusing holy property for personal benefit

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the earlier group of three חטאות. This 'grazing' ruling applies only to the last two cases, and only when the owner has not yet gotten his כפרה.

phrases.english: And if before the owners achieved atonement
phrases.notes: We're still talking about the two cases just mentioned: the חטאת whose year passed, and the lost one that turned up blemished.

phrases.english: it shall graze until it becomes blemished,
and it shall be sold, and they shall buy another with its money.
And it makes a substitute, and one is liable for misusing it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's split ruling for the last two חטאות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the owner has not yet achieved atonement, the animal grazes until it gets a blemish, is sold, and its money buys a new offering. It makes a תמורה and has מעילה.

steps.title: Why does the משנה split only the last cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the first group of חטאות has no split based on the owner's כפרה, while the last group does.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is different about the first part, where the משנה makes no distinction, and what is different about the last part, where it does?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It asks why the משנה treats the first three cases with one rule, but divides the last two cases into 'before כפרה' and 'after כפרה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is not attacking the משנה. It wants to understand how the משנה is built. Why is there a split in the סיפא but not in the רישא?

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (a question asking for the reason behind a difference)
The first part of the משנה
The last part of the משנה
Distinguishes, makes a split between cases

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא דְּלָא קָא מִיפַּלְגִי,
phrases.english: What is different about the first clause, that it does not distinguish,
phrases.notes: 'Distinguish' here means splitting the case into before and after the owner's כפרה.

phrases.english: and what is different about the latter clause, that it does distinguish?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא דְּלָא קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about how the whole משנה is structured
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה splits based on the owner's כפרה only in the סיפא

steps.title: The first cases have one fixed rule; the last ones depend on the situation
steps.stepSummary: The רישא is 'absolute' and always has the same rule. The סיפא is not absolute, so its rule depends on whether the owner already achieved atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first part is clear-cut for the תנא; the last part is not clear-cut for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: in the first three cases the animal always goes to die, no matter what. In the last two, the answer changes depending on the owner's כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The split in the משנה follows the law itself. Where there is only one outcome, there is nothing to divide. Where the outcome depends on whether the owner already got his כפרה, the משנה has to spell out both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: Absolute, clear-cut: one rule with no exceptions

steps.whatToRemember: The first three חטאות always die. The last two depend on whether the owner already achieved atonement, and that is why only they are split.

phrases.english: The first clause is absolute for him,
phrases.notes: 'For him' means for the תנא of the משנה: in his view the rule there never changes.

phrases.english: the latter clause is not absolute for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רישא has one fixed rule, while the סיפא's rule depends on the owner's כפרה

steps.title: This was already taught in מסכת תמורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the משנה already taught this same law in the context of תמורה, so why repeat it here?
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was already taught in connection with substitution!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the same משנה already appears in מסכת תמורה. Repeating it here looks unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה normally doesn't teach the same law twice. So the repetition needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: In connection with, in the section about

phrases.english: But he already taught it in connection with substitution!
phrases.notes: This points to the same משנה in מסכת תמורה (21b).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new question about why the whole משנה is repeated
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that this משנה appears here at all
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A law already taught in מסכת תמורה should not need to be repeated in מסכת מעילה

steps.title: There it is about תמורה; here it is about מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The same law is taught in each place because of that מסכת's own topic: in תמורה for the laws of substitution, and here for the laws of misuse.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it was taught because of substitution; here it is taught because of misuse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each מסכת includes this משנה for its own reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists both rules: whether the animal makes a תמורה, and whether it has מעילה. מסכת תמורה needs it for the תמורה rule. מסכת מעילה needs it for the מעילה rule. So it is not a wasted repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in the other place)
Here
Because of, for the sake of

steps.whatToRemember: The same משנה can appear in two מסכתות, each time for that מסכת's own topic: תמורה there, מעילה here.

phrases.english: He taught it there because of substitution,
he taught it here because of misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different purpose for each place it appears
steps.terutzMaskana: Each מסכת teaches the משנה for its own subject: תמורה there, מעילה here

steps.title: Unassigned money for a נזיר's offerings has no מעילה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that money a נזיר set aside for his offerings, without saying which coins are for which offering, may not be used, but there is no מעילה, because all of it is fit for the שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a person sets aside money for the offerings of his נזירות, one may not benefit from it, but there is no מעילה, because every coin could end up being used for שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a נזיר who put aside one pile of money for his three end-of-נזירות offerings (חטאת, עולה, שלמים) without dividing it up. The משנה says you may not use it, but if you do, there is no מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You may not use the money because some of it might belong to the חטאת or the עולה. Still, there is no מעילה, because any coin you took could be the שלמים money, and שלמים money does not carry מעילה. The doubt removes the penalty, but it does not make the money permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: sets aside (money or an animal) for a קרבן
the vow of being a נזיר; at its end he brings a חטאת, an עולה and a שלמים
you may not benefit from it, but if you do, there is no מעילה
peace offering; there is no מעילה with it before its blood is sprinkled

steps.confusionAlert: 'No מעילה' does not mean 'allowed to use.' The משנה says both things: do not use it, and if you did, there is no מעילה penalty.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who sets aside money for his נזירות offerings —
phrases.notes: He means one pile of money for all three offerings, without saying which coins go to which offering.

phrases.english: one may not benefit from it, but there is no מעילה,
because they are fit
to all be used for שלמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic after the discussion of the conditional חטאות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unassigned money for a נזיר's offerings may not be used, but there is no מעילה, since every coin is fit for the שלמים.

steps.title: The נזיר died: unassigned money and חטאת money
steps.stepSummary: If the נזיר dies, unassigned money goes to gift offerings. Money assigned to the חטאת is thrown into the Dead Sea; one may not use it, but there is no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he died and had unassigned money, it goes to gift offerings. If the money was assigned, the חטאת money goes to the Dead Sea; one may not use it, but there is no מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now covers a נזיר who died before bringing his offerings. It splits the money into two kinds: money he never divided up, and money he did assign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unassigned money cannot be pinned to any one offering, so all of it goes to gift offerings. Once money is clearly marked for the חטאת, it follows the rule for a חטאת whose owner died: it is destroyed, so it is thrown into the Dead Sea. You may not use it, but there is no מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: unassigned money, not marked for any specific offering
assigned money, clearly marked for a specific offering
a gift (voluntary) offering
the Dead Sea, where money is thrown so it is destroyed

phrases.english: If he died and had unassigned money,
it goes to gift offerings.
If it was assigned money:
the money for the חטאת goes to the Dead Sea;
phrases.notes: Throwing it into the Dead Sea is simply a way to destroy it so no one can use it.

phrases.english: one may not benefit from it, but there is no מעילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a new case: the נזיר died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the נזיר dies, unassigned money goes to gift offerings, and assigned חטאת money is destroyed. It may not be used, but it carries no מעילה.

steps.title: The נזיר died: עולה money and שלמים money
steps.stepSummary: Money assigned to the עולה buys a gift עולה and has מעילה. Money assigned to the שלמים buys a שלמים that is eaten for one day and needs no breads.
steps.simpleTranslation: The עולה money is used to bring an עולה, and it has מעילה. The שלמים money is used to bring a שלמים, which is eaten for one day and does not need breads.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the case of the נזיר who died. It explains what happens to the money he had assigned to his עולה and to his שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the חטאת, an עולה and a שלמים can still be brought as gift offerings after the owner dies. The עולה money is fully holy, so it has מעילה. The שלמים keeps the one-day eating limit of a נזיר's שלמים, but it does not need the breads that normally come with it.

keyTerms.meaning: burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
eaten for only one day (and the night after it)
the breads that normally come with a נזיר's שלמים

steps.whatToRemember: Each kind of a נזיר's money follows its own offering. Unassigned money: no מעילה, because any coin could be the שלמים. After death: unassigned money goes to gift offerings, חטאת money is destroyed, עולה money buys an עולה with מעילה, and שלמים money buys a one-day שלמים with no breads.

phrases.english: With the money for the עולה, they bring an עולה,
and there is מעילה with it.
With the money for the שלמים, they bring a שלמים,
and it is eaten for one day,
but it does not need breads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of assigned money after the נזיר's death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After death, עולה money buys an עולה that has מעילה, and שלמים money buys a שלמים eaten for one day, with no breads.

steps.title: ריש לקיש asks why bird offerings were not taught too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with ריש לקיש challenging the משנה: it should also have taught the case of money set aside for bird offerings (קינים). His question is finished in the next step.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: ריש לקיש objected: Let the משנה also teach the case of one who sets aside money for bird offerings —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with ריש לקיש asking why the משנה left out a case that seems similar: money set aside for a pair of bird offerings. This is a setup line, and the full question is finished in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pair of birds is also a set of different offerings (an עולה and a חטאת) paid for from one sum of money. So ריש לקיש wonders why the משנה gave a rule only for a נזיר's money and not for bird money. The next lines will explain what he thinks the משנה should have taught.

keyTerms.meaning: objected to it; raises a strong challenge
let it also teach (the משנה should have included another case)
pairs of bird offerings (literally 'nests'), usually one עולה and one חטאת

phrases.english: GEMARA:
ריש לקיש objected to this:
Let the משנה also teach:
one who sets aside money for bird offerings —

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ וְלִיתְנֵי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא's first move on the new משנה: it questions why the first ruling (step 6) was not also taught for bird offerings.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's choice to teach only the case of a נזיר's unassigned money.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Money for bird offerings also covers more than one kind of offering, so it seems the משנה should have taught that case too. The full argument is spelled out in the next step.

steps.title: Bird-offering money could be bought for unfit birds
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש finishes his challenge. The משנה should have said that bird-offering money may not be used but has no מעילה, because it could buy birds that are unfit for the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not benefit from it, but there is no מעילה, because the money is fit to buy turtledoves that are still too young, or young pigeons that are already too old!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of ריש לקיש's question from the step before. He spells out the ruling he thinks the משנה should have taught about money for bird offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unassigned money has no מעילה because every coin could go toward the שלמים, which has no מעילה. ריש לקיש argues the same way here. Every coin could go toward birds that are not fit for the altar, so this money should also have no מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Turtledoves, which are fit as offerings only once they are grown
Young pigeons, which are fit as offerings only while they are young
Whose time has not yet come (still too young)
Whose time has passed (already too old)

phrases.english: One may not benefit from it, but there is no misuse,
because the coins are fit
to buy turtledoves whose time has not yet come
and young pigeons whose time has passed!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶהֱנִין וְלֹא מוֹעֲלִין, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן רְאוּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes ריש לקיש's challenge that began in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's choice to teach only the case of the נזיר's unassigned money
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unassigned money has no מעילה because it could all buy a שלמים. By the same reasoning, bird money could all buy unfit birds, so the משנה should have taught that case too.

steps.title: The Torah never says to bring unfit birds
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains why the two cases are different. For unassigned money, the Torah itself says to bring a שלמים. The Torah never tells anyone to bring birds that are unfit for the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: With unassigned money, the Torah said, 'Bring a שלמים.' Did the Torah say, 'Bring turtledoves that are still too young'? Those are not fit for the altar!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers ריש לקיש by showing that the two cases are not alike. That is why the משנה did not need to teach the bird case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The unassigned money really is meant for a שלמים, an offering the Torah asks the נזיר to bring. That is why it shares the שלמים's lack of מעילה. Unfit birds are not a real use the money is meant for, so they cannot take away this money's מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Unassigned money, set aside without saying which coins are for which offering
Fit to be offered on the altar

steps.whatToRemember: Money gets the status of an offering only if the Torah actually calls for that offering. Something the money could buy in theory, like unfit birds, does not count.

phrases.english: Rava said:
With unassigned money, the Torah said:
bring a peace offering,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה: הָבֵא תּוֹרִין שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ זְמַנָּן?
phrases.english: Did the Torah say: bring turtledoves whose time has not yet come?
They are not fit for the altar!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה בְּמָעוֹת סְתוּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's challenge from steps 9 and 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the two cases are different
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any use the money could be put to, even buying unfit birds, should cancel its מעילה, just as the שלמים does.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a use the Torah actually commands, like the שלמים, has this effect. Unfit birds are not such a use, so the bird case is not comparable.

steps.title: Blood and libations work in opposite directions
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. רבי שמעון teaches a general rule: blood is lenient at first and strict at the end, while נסכים are strict at first and lenient at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי שמעון says: Blood is lenient at the start and strict at the end. נסכים are strict at the start and lenient at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with רבי שמעון's short, general rule. The next lines of the משנה will explain what he means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Lenient' and 'strict' here mean whether there is מעילה. רבי שמעון points out that blood and נסכים are mirror images of each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Lenient, here meaning there is no מעילה
Strict, here meaning there is מעילה
Libations: wine poured on the altar along with offerings
The start and the end of the item's use in the מקדש

phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Shimon says:
The blood is lenient at the start
and strict at its end.
Libations are strict at their start
and lenient at their end.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: הַדָּם קַל בַּתְּחִלָּה וְחָמוּר בְּסוֹפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood: no מעילה at first, מעילה later. נסכים: מעילה at first, no מעילה later.

steps.title: When exactly blood and libations have misuse
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains its rule. Blood has no מעילה at first but does once it flows out to the קדרון valley. נסכים have מעילה at first but not once they go down into the pits under the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blood, at the start: there is no מעילה. Once it went out to the קדרון stream, there is מעילה. נסכים, at the start: there is מעילה. Once they went down into the pits: there is no מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains its general rule by naming the exact point where each item's status changes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For blood, the turning point is when the leftover blood leaves the מקדש and reaches נחל קדרון. From then on there is מעילה. For נסכים, the turning point is when they go down into the שיתין. From then on there is no more מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: There is מעילה: using it counts as misusing holy property
The קדרון valley below the Temple Mount, where the leftover blood flowed out
The pits or drainpipes under the altar that the libations flowed into

steps.confusionAlert: It can seem backwards that blood becomes more strict after it has left the altar. Just learn the משנה's rule as it is written here for now.
steps.whatToRemember: Blood: no מעילה until it reaches נחל קדרון, then מעילה. נסכים: מעילה until they reach the שיתין, then none.

phrases.english: Blood, at its start: there is no misuse with it.
Once it went out to the Kidron stream, there is misuse with it.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the leftover blood, which flowed through a channel out of the מקדש down to the valley.

phrases.english: Libations, at their start: there is misuse with them.
Once they went down into the pits, there is no misuse with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the general rule from step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood has מעילה only once it reaches נחל קדרון. נסכים lose their מעילה once they go down into the שיתין.

steps.title: A ברייתא: a dispute over מעילה with blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון say there is מעילה with blood. The חכמים say there is no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A ברייתא teaches: One is liable for misusing blood. This is the view of רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון. The חכמים say: one is not liable for misusing it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא records a dispute about whether using blood of קרבנות counts as מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said blood has מעילה once it flows out to the קדרון valley. This ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון hold that view, but the חכמים disagree and say blood never has מעילה. This sets up the next question: what is the חכמים' source?

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of the קרבנות
The Sages, here the majority view that disagrees

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Sages taught:
One is liable for misusing blood,
phrases.notes: Based on the משנה just before, this means the blood once it has flowed out to the קדרון valley.

phrases.english: the words of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Shimon.
And the Sages say: one is not liable for misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that relates to the משנה's ruling that blood has מעילה after reaching the קדרון valley, and shows a dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון: blood has מעילה. חכמים: blood has no מעילה.

steps.title: What is the source for saying blood has no מעילה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the חכמים' view that there is no מעילה with blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the one who says there is no מעילה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the חכמים hold that blood has no מעילה. This question sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood comes from a consecrated animal, so one might expect it to be הקדש like the rest of the קרבן. The גמרא wants to know what source takes blood out of the rules of מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
The one who says (a certain view)

phrases.english: What is the reason
of the one who says one is not liable for misuse?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין מוֹעֲלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the חכמים' view in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the view that blood has no מעילה.

steps.title: עולא: the blood was given "to you"
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers from the פסוק "ואני נתתיו לכם": the blood is yours, so it does not belong to הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The פסוק says, "And I have given it to you," which means it is yours.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives the first answer. The words "to you" in the פסוק teach that the blood belongs to the people, not to הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעילה only applies to things that belong to הקדש. If the Torah calls the blood "yours," it is not הקדש property, so using it cannot be מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: I have given it to you
It is yours

phrases.english: Ulla said: The verse says:
"And I have given it to you"
– it is yours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "לכם" teaches that the blood belongs to the people, not to הקדש, so there is no מעילה.

steps.title: The school of רבי ישמעאל: given for atonement, not for מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל learns from the word "לכפר" that blood was given for atonement and not to be subject to מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: "To atone" means I gave it for atonement, and not for מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source from the same פסוק. The word "to atone" shows the blood's only purpose is כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא focused on "to you"; this teaching focuses on "to atone." Since the Torah limits the blood's role to כפרה, it is not treated as הקדש property for מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: To atone
Atonement

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"To atone" – I gave it for atonement,
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, ויקרא 17:11: "I have given it to you on the altar to atone for your souls."

phrases.english: and not for misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source for the same ruling, from a different word in the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "לכפר" limits the blood's purpose to atonement, excluding it from מעילה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: blood is the same before and after atonement
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן learns from the word "הוא" that blood keeps one status. Just as after the כפרה it has no מעילה, so too before the כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The פסוק says, "For it is the blood that atones by reason of the life." Before atonement it is like after atonement. Just as after atonement there is no מעילה, so too before atonement there is no מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a third source. He reads the word "הוא" ("it is") as teaching that the blood stays the same before and after its כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the blood is sprinkled its job is done, so it has no מעילה. רבי יוחנן uses "הוא" to compare the earlier stage to the later one, so the blood has no מעילה before the כפרה too.

keyTerms.meaning: Before the atonement (before the blood is sprinkled)
After the atonement (after the blood is sprinkled)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The verse says:
"For it is the blood that atones by reason of the life"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:11. The key word is הוא, "it is," meaning the blood stays as it is.

phrases.english: – before atonement it is like after atonement.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְאַחַר כַּפָּרָה אֵין בּוֹ מְעִילָה,
phrases.english: Just as after atonement it has no misuse,

phrases.aramaic: אַף לִפְנֵי כַפָּרָה אֵין בּוֹ מְעִילָה.
phrases.english: so too before atonement it has no misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the same ruling, based on comparing the blood's two stages.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "הוא" equates the blood before and after כפרה; since after כפרה there is no מעילה, there is none before either.

steps.title: Why not compare the other way?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: if the two stages are equal, maybe we should say blood has מעילה before the כפרה and so also after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: just as before atonement it has מעילה, so too after atonement it has מעילה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's comparison. It argues the comparison could just as easily run in the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's פסוק only says the two stages are equal; it does not say which stage sets the rule. Before the כפרה the blood is part of a consecrated קרבן and would normally have מעילה, so why not apply that to after the כפרה too?

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead (proposing the opposite reading)
It is subject to מעילה

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the halacha is that blood has מעילה. It is only showing that רבי יוחנן's comparison alone could point either way, and an answer will follow.

phrases.english: But say instead:

phrases.aramaic: מַה לִפְנֵי כַפָּרָה – יֵשׁ בּוֹ מְעִילָה,
phrases.english: just as before atonement – it has misuse,

phrases.aramaic: אַף לְאַחַר כַּפָּרָה – יֵשׁ בּוֹ מְעִילָה!
phrases.english: so too after atonement – it has misuse!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: מַה לִפְנֵי כַפָּרָה יֵשׁ בּוֹ מְעִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the direction of רבי יוחנן's comparison in step 18.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An equation of two stages can be read in either direction. Since blood before כפרה is part of a consecrated קרבן, the comparison could make it have מעילה after כפרה as well.

steps.title: Once the מצוה is done, there is no more מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge with a rhetorical question: nothing still has מעילה after its מצוה is done. So the comparison can only run from 'no מעילה after' to 'no מעילה before.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really anything whose מצוה has already been done and it still has מעילה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 19 with a rhetorical question. Blood cannot have מעילה after the כפרה, because its מצוה is already finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 suggested reading רבי יוחנן's comparison the other way: מעילה before the כפרה, and so also after. The גמרא rejects this because of a general rule: once a holy item's מצוה is done, it no longer has מעילה. So 'after the כפרה' is fixed as no מעילה, and the 'before' stage must match it.

keyTerms.meaning: Its מצוה has been done, meaning the holy item has already served its purpose
'Is it really so...?' This opens a rhetorical question that expects the answer 'no'

steps.confusionAlert: This line is a question in form, but it is really an answer. It means 'there is no such thing,' and it rejects the challenge from Step 19.

phrases.english: Is there really anything
whose מצוה has already been done
phrases.notes: For the blood, its מצוה is the כפרה, which is the sprinkling on the מזבח.

phrases.english: and it still has מעילה?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי יֵשׁ לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁנַּעֲשֵׂית מִצְוָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19 and defends רבי יוחנן's direction of comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: General principle: once a מצוה is done, there is no מעילה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe blood has מעילה both before and after the כפרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: After the כפרה there is certainly no מעילה, so before the כפרה there is none either.

steps.title: Why not? Questioning the rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule from Step 20 and asks why an item could not still have מעילה after its מצוה is done.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not? Why couldn't something still have מעילה after its מצוה is done?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the rule it just used. It asks why we should assume that a finished מצוה always ends מעילה. This sets up a search for a case where it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 rested completely on the rule 'no מעילה after the מצוה is done.' If that rule is not universal, Step 20's answer falls apart. Then the challenge from Step 19 comes back: maybe blood has מעילה both before and after.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Why not?' A challenge to an assumption that was just taken for granted

phrases.english: Why not?!
phrases.notes: The גמרא is hinting that there may be a case where something has מעילה even after its מצוה is done.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the general principle that Step 20's answer relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule from Step 20 that nothing has מעילה after its מצוה is done
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule was simply assumed. If even one case exists where מעילה continues after the מצוה is done, the defense of רבי יוחנן fails.
